newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DANE OLSEN TO REPLACE VAN GAAL AS AJAX COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DANE OLSEN TO REPLACE VAN GAAL AS AJAX COACH.

text.p: Former Danish international Morten Olsen will replace Louis van Gaal as coach at Dutch champions Ajax Amsterdam in the new season, Dutch daily Algemeen Dagblad said on Wednesday.
The paper said the club, European champions in 1995 and beaten finalists last season, would announce the decision on Thursday when the squad returns from training in Spain.
Olsen, 47, who played a record 102 games for Denmark, has had a brief and undistinguished managerial career.
He coached Danish club Brondby for two seasons before joining German first division side FC Cologne in 1992 -- the club where he ended his playing career aged almost 40.
After four seasons in charge and still no trophy, Olsen was sacked in 1995.
The hugely successful Van Gaal announced late last year that he planned to leave Ajax and head for fresh challenges, hinting that he would seek a coaching job outside The Netherlands.
Van Gaal's decision prompted a flurry of speculation as to his likely successor, but illustrious names like Johan Cruyff, Marco van Basten and Kevin Keegan were overlooked by the Ajax board.
Olson began his playing career at Vordingborg BK in Denmark, before moving to Nykoping and then to Cercle Brugge, Molenbeek and Anderlecht in Belgium, ending a long and successful career at Cologne.
No-one at Ajax was immediately available to comment, but a receptionist said she had read the newspaper report.
